source: Prek Leap National School of Agriculture - "Banana Varieties Giving High Yield and Good Taste Quality" (ពូជចេកផ្តល់ទិន្នផលខ្ពស់ និងគុណភាពសជាតិ) variety trial report, January 2007
text:
Among the growth traits the trial measured, three are reported here with confidence based on the report's own written summaries (rather than the raw per-plant numeric tables, which involve small hand-written Khmer numerals that carry higher risk of misreading and are not transcribed in this pass).

Plant height at data collection: the shortest was accession #12 (GCTCV-119) at 1.59 m; the tallest was #25, the Chek Namva local check, at 3.52 m; the average across all 26 accessions was 2.42 m. Leaf length: shortest was accession #15 (TMBx 5295-1, second accession) at 0.94 m; longest was #11 (FHIA-23) at 1.73 m; average across all 26 accessions was 1.31 m - notably, none of the three local Cambodian checks had the shortest leaves, and Namva had the longest of all. Leaf count per plant: fewest was #25 (Chek Namva) at 22 leaves; most was #2 (FHIA-01) at 37.5 leaves; average across all 26 accessions was about 30 leaves.
